name: GUSINSKY
description: Concurred, argued that law enforcement officers qualify as victims under Marsy's Law and are entitled to request redaction of their names and initials from public filings, but a balancing test is required against other constitutional rights.

name: KERN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the jury district combining Buffalo and Brule Counties did not violate the state or federal constitutions regarding a fair cross-section of the community or the "county or district" requirement.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the court should reach the merits of the case despite the unusual procedural posture regarding defaulted habeas claims, reserving the procedural default issue for future consideration.

name: DEVANEY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court erred by not applying the Nixon factors to the subpoena duces tecum and that E.H. did not waive her right to privacy, as the subpoena lacked the necessary specificity.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, § 12 does not prohibit all contracts between legislators and the State, overruling Asphalt Surfacing and Pitts because general appropriation bills only allocate money and do not authorize specific contracts for ordinary expenses.

name: KERN, Justice
description: Dissented in part and concurred in part, argued that the majority wrongly overrules decades of precedent by exempting general appropriations from Article III, § 12, and that "any law" includes general appropriations, but joined the holding that Article III, § 12 applies to laws passed during a legislator's term.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred specially, arguing that while Amendment A violated the single-subject rule, the court should leave open the question of whether such a violation always renders an entire amendment void, suggesting separability might be appropriate in some cases.

name: MYREN, Justice
description: Dissented in part, arguing that Amendment A contained a single subject because its propositions were incidental to and necessarily connected with the comprehensive plan for legalizing, regulating, and taxing marijuana and related substances, and therefore did not violate Article XXIII, § 1.

name: JENSEN, Chief Justice
description: Concurred with the majority decision to dismiss the inverse condemnation and excessive force claims, and to remand the unlawful entry claim for further proceedings.

name: KERN, Justice
description: Concurred that the inverse condemnation claim should be dismissed and the unlawful entry claim should proceed, but dissented from dismissing the excessive force claim, arguing summary judgment was improper.

name: SALTER, Justice
description: Concurred with the majority opinion on all issues.

name: DEVANEY, Justice
description: Concurred that the inverse condemnation claim should be dismissed and the unlawful entry claim should proceed, but dissented from dismissing the excessive force claim.

name: GILBERTSON, Retired Chief Justice
description: Dissented from the decision to remand the unlawful entry claim, arguing that qualified immunity should have been decided at summary judgment, but concurred with the dismissal of the inverse condemnation and excessive force claims.

name: MYREN, Justice
description: Did not participate as not a member of the Court at the time this action was submitted.
